item.title: Apimondia: Official Visit of the President to Romania and Moldova
item.dc:creator: Matteo Giusti
item.description:
The Acting President of Apimondia, Peter Kozmus, has concluded a five-day official visit to Romania and Moldova, where he met with representatives of the beekeeping sectors in both countries.
The visit included meetings, a conference, and technical tours of beekeeping operations, an educational institution, and honey processing facilities. These activities provided valuable opportunities to strengthen cooperation between Apimondia and local beekeepers and industry stakeholders, exchange experiences, and renew the invitation to participate in the 50th Apimondia International Apicultural Congress in Dubai.
One of the highlights of the visit was a presentation and discussion session hosted by the Romanian Beekeepers Association, attended by the Slovenian and Austrian ambassadors. The meeting underlined the importance of international cooperation in beekeeping and opened discussions on the possibility of Romania hosting a future Apimondia International Apicultural Congress.
The visit was initiated and organised by BeeScience, whose efforts helped bring together key representatives of the beekeeping community and strengthen ties between Apimondia and the beekeeping sectors in Romania and Moldova.

item.title: Brazil, More Beehives to Mitigate El Niño Effects
item.dc:creator: Matteo Giusti
item.description:

item.content:encoded:
It is blooming season in Brazilian apple orchards, a crucial period for pollination and, consequently, for fruit production.

This year, however, climate-related challenges are causing concern. According to ABRAFRUTAS, the Brazilian Association of Fruit Producers and Exporters, lower temperatures last winter favoured the breaking of dormancy in apple trees. In addition, the accumulation of chilling hours in the main producing regions, such as Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina, was above the historical average, contributing to uniform flowering and strong production potential.

However, heavy rainfall associated with El Niño is now raising concerns about pollination. As a result, farmers are renting more beehives to support apple pollination and make the most of the drier days during the blooming period.

Read more on the ABRAFRUTAS magazine here.
